articles.title: Boehly and Walter sell Chelsea shares as Clearlake Capital takes full control of club
articles.summary: American chair Boehly leaves role after deal is secured. ‘I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned’ Todd Boehly and Mark Walter have sold their stakes in Chelsea in a deal under which Clearlake Capital takes full control of the Premier League club.
body: The American billionaire businessmen Boehly and Walter were two of the investors who partnered with Clearlake to buy the club from Roman Abramovich in a sale mandated by the UK government in May 2022. The private equity company Clearlake had previously owned 61.5% of the club, with Boehly and Walter carving up the remaining shares with another investor, Hansjörg Wyss.

A statement issued late on Wednesday night read: “Chelsea Football Club today announced affiliates of Clearlake Capital Group, LP will acquire the ownership interest of Todd Boehly. Hansjorg Wyss will remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group.
“As part of the transition, Clearlake will also acquire Mark Walter’s ownership interest and therefore acquire full control of the club.”

Chelsea said Boehly, the chair, had shown “unwavering commitment” to the ownership group’s belief that the supporters are at the heart of the club. “The owners have worked together with the shared objective of building a sustainable foundation for long-term sporting success,” the statement added.

articles.title: ‘We can’t accept that’: Carrick urges Manchester United to respond after cup collapse
articles.summary: ‘I take responsibility … it doesn’t feel good at the moment’ United beaten 3-2 by Brighton after taking two-goal lead. Michael Carrick admitted Manchester United’s Carabao Cup capitulation against Brighton that was greeted by boos at Old Trafford was unacceptable and that answers had to be found at…
body: United were knocked out 3-2 by Fabian Hürzeler’s visitors after leading 2-0 after 10 minutes through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount. Goals from Charalampos Kostoulas in first‑half added time, Pascal Gross on 65 minutes and Maxim De Cuyper four minutes later eliminated United.
It was the first time United had lost after leading 2-0 at Old Trafford for 50 years and the first time since 1984 they had been defeated there after being ahead at half-time.
Carrick’s side have beaten only Ipswich in the league and Sabah in the Champions League. “Under pressure? That doesn’t bother me one bit,” he said.

“I understand what goes on and how the world works. What bothers me is winning games and I believe we will do, but we have to do it pretty quickly. We can’t accept that [the manner of the defeat] as a group. I take responsibility for it. The performance towards the end of the second half, that’s on me. We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches. It doesn’t feel good at the moment.”

articles.title: Boehly and Walter sell Chelsea stakes to Clearlake
articles.summary: Clearlake Capital acquires full control of Chelsea as chairman Todd Boehly, director Mark Walter and Hansjorg Wyss sell their stakes in the club.
body: Chelsea chairman Todd Boehly and director Mark Walter have sold their stakes in the club to majority owner Clearlake Capital.
Swiss billionaire Hansjorg Wyss has also sold his stake, meaning Clearlake - led by co-founders Behdad Eghbali and Jose E. Feliciano - have now acquired full control of the club.
Boehly, Walter and Wyss each had a 12.8% stake, with Clearlake previously owning 61.5% of the Blues.

American Boehly will leave his role as chairman, a position he has held since 2022, when the consortium bought the club for £2.3bn from Roman Abramovich, who was sanctioned by the UK government in March 2022 over alleged links to Russian president Vladimir Putin - something he has denied.

articles.title: Raphinha cashes in against Santander with hat-trick as Barça hit seven
articles.summary: Cancelo, Jesus and Lamine Yamal also score in rout. Atlético Madrid thrash Osasuna 4-0 to move into third. Raphinha scored a hat-trick as Barcelona ripped Racing Santander to shreds in a spectacular 7-2 triumph in La Liga on Wednesday.
body: João Cancelo, Gabriel Jesus and Lamine Yamal also scored for the unstoppable Catalan giants, who have netted 33 goals in those seven games across all competitions, and who moved three points clear of Real Madrid at the top of La Liga.

With lightning flashing above the Camp Nou, Barça started at rapid pace and took the lead with a thunderbolt from Cancelo. The defender crashed a shot in off the crossbar from long range in the eighth minute.

Dani Olmo twice came close before Raphinha won and converted a penalty for Barça’s second. The Brazilian was clumsily brought down by Pedro Felipe and thrashed the spot-kick into the bottom right corner.

Santander pulled one back when Maguette Gueye barged his way through and produced a neat finish to beat Joan García in goal. However, it proved only brief respite, with Cancelo provoking the third with another long-range effort which deflected in off Asier Villalibre.

articles.title: De Cuyper and Brighton pile on pain for Manchester United with comeback
articles.summary: Across four days Manchester United have lost the 199th derby against Manchester City, were told by JJ Gabriel that he wants to leave, and now they have been knocked out of the Carabao Cup by Brighton.
body: Capitulating after being 2-0 up may be the pick of these dizzying blows, as the prolonged boos at the final whistle suggested, and doing so ends a proud 50-year record: the last time the same lead at Old Trafford ended in defeat was Tottenham’s 3-2 win in September 1976.
When Marcus Rashford skated in with the chance to take the tie to 3-3 late on, there was no surprise he hit Jason Steele rather than the net.

Towards the end, Matheus Cunha was thrown on to join Bruno Fernandes, also a late substitute, illustrating how desperate Michael Carrick was. Yet Charalampos Kostoulas went close to scoring a second for Brighton, as United could not find a route to cancelling out Maxim De Cuyper’s 69th-minute strike that proved the winner.

After taking only four points from 12 in the league, serious questions will now be asked about where Carrick’s team are heading; they have to beat Fulham on Sunday to start correcting a dismal start to the season. The manager already looks haunted and he talked afterwards of not caring about being under pressure.

articles.title: Alex Afari is ready to go vs. Texas A&M, per Will Stein
articles.summary: The Kentucky Wildcats are preparing for a date with Texas A&M in College Station this Saturday, and it appears the defense could be getting an important piece back to help slow down Marcel Reed and the Aggies offense.
body: During his Wednesday coaches show, head coach Will Stein announced that fifth-year linebacker Alex Afari is ready to roll, as he continues to gear up for the Aggies while working through his eligibility battle.
On his weekly radio show, Kentucky HC Will Stein says LB Alex Afari is ready to roll this week, and his role has been expanding.

Afari logged three snaps in Week 1, then was surprisingly held out of last week’s loss to Alabama, despite Stein saying the plan was for the linebacker to play. So, we do have to take these comments with a grain of salt until we actually see Afari out on the field when Kentucky takes on the Aggies.

The defense has been quite impressive to start the season, and adding an experienced player like Afari to that unit will only help as SEC play ramps up. With a dynamic backfield in Reed and Ruben Owens, Jay Bateman will need big plays from his defense if they hope to pull off the upset. Afari adds that playmaking, plus the experience needed when headed into environments like the 12th Man.

articles.title: Painful endgame for Gray as stale Hibs slump
articles.summary: A club hero, David Gray ends his time as Hibs head coach not to the sound of euphoria from fans, but to the sound of a support collectively exhaling in relief, writes Tom English.
body: It was the strangest kind of farewell; more sadness than satisfaction, more 'thanks for the memories' than 'never darken our door again'.

After a dozen years as a player, a goalscoring and Scottish Cup-winning icon, a coach, an interim manager and, for the last two-and-a-bit seasons, the first team manager, David Gray exited Hibernian on Wednesday evening.

He left, not to the sound of euphoria from the fans, but to the sound of a support collectively exhaling in relief. Given what he did on an immortal day at Hampden in 2016, no Hibs supporter wanted to boo the man they called Sir David Gray, nobody wanted to call for his head. It was a painful endgame, for everybody.

Hibs have sacked many managers in recent seasons, but this was no Nick Montgomery, no Lee Johnson, no Shaun Maloney. Gray was altogether different. Driven, passionate, honest as the day is long, brutally so when talking about how things were going wrong, which he had been doing too much of lately.

articles.title: Reds stop Dodgers in their tracks in 6-2 defeat
articles.summary: The Dodgers needed one win to clinch their 13th NL West title since 2013. Instead, they were forced to go with an impromptu bullpen game, and the Cincinnati Reds slugged their way to a 6-2 victory on Wednesday.
body: The Dodgers created havoc on the base paths in the first inning, as a single and two walks helped load the bases against left-hander Andrew Abbot, but Miguel Rojas flew out to center field to keep the game scoreless.

In his first start at Great American Ball Park since tossing a no-hitter with the San Francisco Giants in 2024, Blake Snell allowed a two-out single to Sal Stewart, only to pick him off trying to advance to second base in a scoreless first inning. That inning was all that Snell could go on Wednesday, as he ended up leaving early due to left groin tightness, leaving the bullpen to do the heavy lifting. Blake Treinen worked around a leadoff baserunner in a scoreless second inning in replacement of Snell.
After Mookie Betts connected for his second single against Abbot in the third inning, Will Smith brought home the game’s first run with an RBI double off the base of the right-center field wall.

articles.title: Leicestershire on brink of relegation after 27-point deduction
articles.summary: Leicestershire are on the brink of relegation from County Championship Division One after being deducted 27 points for breaching pitch regulations.
body: The points penalty imposed by the independent Cricket Discipline Panel (CDP) midway through their penultimate match of the season meant the Foxes have dropped to the bottom of the table.

In his interview with the Cricket Regulator before the tribunal hearing, Leicestershire's head groundsman Callum Lewin said there were "circumstances leading up to the game that were just out of my control".

They included an "unscheduled Bollywood filming event" taking place at Uptonsteel Grace Road four days before the start of the match, while Lewin also referenced the exceptionally hot weather in the build-up as another possible reason for the pitch being dry.

Leicestershire's punishment consists of the loss of all 19 points earned in the win over Glamorgan, an extra eight-point penalty and a £5,000 fine. A further eight-point deduction has been suspended for a year.

articles.title: New season, same Man Utd story - Carrick is now firmly feeling the pressure
articles.summary: This wasn't just a defeat. This wasn't just a collapse. This wasn't just a cup exit. Another Manchester United managerial project is heading in that one, same direction. And even Michael Carrick recognises that.
body: "We've gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that," he said. "I'm happy enough to be honest about that. That's how it feels."

It's a story that's been seen before. A dismal Carabao Cup experience at the first hurdle - this time throwing away a 2-0 lead to exit to Brighton - harks back to memories of Ruben Amorim's disappointing defeat at Grimsby last year, which helped signal the beginning of the end.

A cup exit to the Seagulls was also reminiscent of the FA Cup defeat United suffered to Fabian Hurzeler's side at the start of the year. That was the last match before Carrick returned to the club and sparked a mini-revival. Now it seems like United are back to square one again.

Even Pascal Gross scoring the equaliser at Old Trafford brought back memories of how he netted twice at United's home in August 2022 to put Erik ten Hag's tenure on the back foot, in the same way Carrick is facing an uphill battle now.

articles.title: LSU QB Sam Leavitt 'doubtful' on injury report ahead of Ole Miss showdown, did not throw in latest practice
articles.summary: Leavitt's surprising status -- which CBS Sports reports stems from an upper body injury -- adds another intriguing storyline to Lane Kiffin's anticipated first trip back to Oxford
body: LSU listed quarterback Sam Leavitt as doubtful on its first injury report ahead of this weekend's game at Ole Miss.
Leavitt is dealing with an upper body injury and he did not throw in Wednesday's practice, CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz reports.

Leavitt did not appear to be injured in last week's win over Louisiana Tech, where he rebounded from a three-interception first half with 366 total yards and four total touchdowns. LSU only led Louisiana Tech by a single possession last weekend at halftime, a result of turnover-filled first two quarters inside Tiger Stadium.

"Sam's gotta do a better job taking care of the ball," Kiffin said in the aftermath. "We made a lot of yards, and we were smooth through that at times, but obviously, the red zone is where you gotta finish drives. So maybe it was perfect for us that we needed something like that, 'cause it's a game we play good on offense in games."
